task_3.title: Rename default branch references from master to main
task_3.description: Version 1.8.1 updates user-facing references to the project's default Git branch so documentation and release guidance use `main` instead of `master`. No runtime library behavior changes are indicated by the release note or code diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that user-facing references to the project's default Git branch use `main` instead of `master`, so users following repository or contribution guidance are directed to the correct branch.

expectation.grounded: The 1.8.1 update should reflect the repository default branch rename from `master` to `main` anywhere this branch name is presented to users. Based on the release note and the absence of code changes, this update does not introduce runtime API, CLI, or library behavior changes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should consistently see the current default branch name in upgrade notes and related guidance, and any instructions that depend on the default branch should point to `main`.

constraints.grounded: Do not imply changes to public runtime functionality, error behavior, or package interfaces. The scope is limited to the visible branch-name reference change described in the release note.
constraints.conceptual: This update should only correct the branch naming presented to users and should not alter how the library behaves in normal use.

behavior: User-facing references to the repository default branch are updated from `master` to `main`.
No observable runtime behavior changes are introduced as part of this 1.8.1 update.
acceptance_criteria: When users read upgrade or repository guidance affected by this change, it should identify `main` as the default branch.
When users follow branch-specific instructions derived from the updated guidance, they should no longer be directed to `master` as the default branch.
Upgrading from 1.8.0 to 1.8.1 should not change runtime library behavior, public APIs, or command behavior.

task_2.title: Gracefully handle repositories that reject negative wheel range requests
task_2.description: The 1.8.1 update makes lazy wheel inspection more resilient when a package repository does not support HTTP suffix byte-range requests. Instead of aborting on unexpected error responses from the initial negative-offset probe, dependency processing falls back to a safer size lookup path and continues, while preserving the existing behavior for true range-size overflow responses.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that lazy wheel inspection continues to work when a package repository rejects negative HTTP range requests with unexpected error responses, rather than failing dependency resolution.

expectation.grounded: During lazy wheel inspection, if the initial negative byte-range request for the end of a wheel file raises an HTTPError other than `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable`, the operation should treat that domain as not supporting negative range requests, obtain the content length through a non-negative-range lookup, and continue without surfacing that HTTP error. A `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` response should still be interpreted as an oversized suffix request and should continue to use `Content-Range` to determine the full file length.
expectation.conceptual: When a repository does not correctly support suffix range requests for wheel files, package metadata retrieval should gracefully fall back to a compatible path and continue resolving dependencies. Servers that are only indicating that the requested suffix is larger than the file should keep the prior successful behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for repositories that already support negative byte-range requests. Preserve the existing `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` handling, and once a domain is identified as not supporting negative suffix ranges, avoid retrying that unsupported probe again during the same dependency resolution run.
constraints.conceptual: Keep normal lazy wheel behavior unchanged for compliant repositories and for ordinary small-file range handling. The fix should only broaden compatibility for repositories that answer unsupported suffix range probes with unexpected HTTP errors.

behavior: The initial suffix range probe for lazy wheel inspection no longer fails immediately on non-`416` HTTP errors from repositories that reject negative offsets.
Any non-`416` HTTP error from that initial negative-range request triggers a fallback path that determines wheel size without relying on a negative range response.
`416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` continues to mean the requested suffix exceeded the wheel size, and the full file length is still derived from the `Content-Range` response header.

After a repository is recognized as not supporting negative suffix ranges, later lazy wheel operations against the same domain in the same dependency resolution run should skip that unsupported probe.
acceptance_criteria: When lazy wheel inspection targets a repository that returns an HTTP error such as `500`, `405`, or `501` for the initial suffix range request, dependency processing should continue through a fallback lookup instead of failing with that HTTP error.
When the initial suffix range request receives `416 Requested Range Not Satisfiable` with a valid `Content-Range`, the resolver should continue by using the reported full wheel size.

When the same repository is accessed again during the same dependency resolution run after a negative-range rejection has been observed, lazy wheel inspection should avoid issuing the unsupported negative suffix range request again.

task_1.title: Require packaging 23.1+ for Poetry metadata handling
task_1.description: Poetry 1.8.1 raises its minimum runtime dependency on packaging from 20.5 to 23.1 so installations cannot keep an older packaging release that lacks the metadata API Poetry already uses. This aligns the declared compatibility floor with actual runtime behavior and prevents metadata-related command failures caused by an outdated packaging version.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Poetry 1.8.1 also upgrades the runtime packaging dependency to a version that supports Poetry's metadata parsing paths, so metadata-driven operations do not fail because packaging.metadata is unavailable.

expectation.grounded: Poetry 1.8.1 must declare and resolve packaging >=23.1 instead of the previous >=20.5 floor. This requirement is necessary because Poetry runtime code imports packaging.metadata APIs, including parse_email and RawMetadata, during package inspection and repository metadata parsing. Environments that leave Poetry paired with packaging <23.1 must no longer be considered compatible, and supported metadata-reading flows should not raise ModuleNotFoundError due to a missing packaging.metadata module.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, Poetry should only run with packaging versions that provide the metadata functionality it depends on. Users should not need to manually discover and fix an outdated transitive dependency before metadata-based Poetry operations work.

constraints.grounded: This patch must remain a dependency-compatibility fix rather than a change to Poetry's metadata feature set. Existing supported metadata inspection behavior should remain intact; the main change is that unsupported packaging versions below 23.1 are excluded up front instead of failing later at runtime.
constraints.conceptual: The release should preserve normal metadata-related behavior for supported environments while preventing dependency combinations that are known to break at runtime.

behavior: The minimum supported packaging version changes from >=20.5 to >=23.1.
Poetry 1.8.1 no longer treats packaging versions below 23.1 as valid runtime dependencies.
Metadata inspection and parsing flows that depend on packaging.metadata are protected from missing-module failures caused by an outdated packaging installation.
acceptance_criteria: Given an environment where packaging 21.x or 23.0 is already installed, when Poetry is upgraded to 1.8.1, that packaging version should no longer satisfy Poetry's declared runtime dependency.
When Poetry 1.8.1 performs wheel or repository metadata inspection, it should not fail because the installed packaging version lacks packaging.metadata.
When users install Poetry 1.8.1 through normal dependency resolution, the resolved packaging version should be 23.1 or newer.
